quotes: "Scholars who want to research a scientific topic must take time to read, extract meaning, and identify connections across many papers." (p. 1)

"The Relatedly system presents users with related work paragraphs from prior work on a topic and scaffolds the paragraph exploration experience with features for reading, prioritization, and progress tracking." (p. 2)
"We compared Relatedly to a Baseline system simulating standard scholarly search engines as an within-subject condition." (p. 10)
"Many design decisions were influenced by our focus on literature review of scientific topics by scholars." (p. 16)

mechanisms.value: query-ranked related-work paragraph overview across papers
mechanisms.what_makes_it_separate: this is the broad entry representation of topic-spanning paragraph cards; it does not itself label their gist, open relational drill-downs, or record exploration state.

quotes: "Given a search query, Relatedly presents a list of related work paragraphs relevant to the query in the Overview View (Figure 1)." (p. 6)

entries.value: query-ranked related-work paragraph overview across papers

quotes: "Each paragraph is representative of a different subtopic and is ranked to cover a broad range of subtopics." (p. 6)

mechanisms.value: author-derived or BART-generated paragraph subtopic labels
mechanisms.value_canonical: VA097 Condensed summary of a single item
mechanisms.what_makes_it_separate: these labels externalize each paragraph’s gist and support skimming; the paragraph overview remains usable as a list even when this labeling operation is absent.

quotes: "Descriptive paragraph headings: Each paragraph in the Overview View comes with a descriptive title to describe the gist of the paragraph’s focus and serve as a subtopic for the user." (p. 7)

quotes: "For paragraphs for which authors had only written generic or short section headings that contained less information (e.g. “Related Work” or “Fact-Checking”), or for paragraphs with no section headings, Relatedly generates descriptive titles using a BART-based [42] model (described in more detail in §4.3)." (p. 7)

mechanisms.value_canonical: VA012 Drill-down from summary to underlying instances
mechanisms.what_makes_it_separate: it traverses relations from one selected paragraph into a focused comparison set, whereas the overview presents breadth without requiring a selected anchor.

quotes: "Similar paragraphs given a paragraph: In the Similar Paragraphs View, a list of similar paragraphs are shown for a selected paragraph." (p. 7)

quotes: "We determine paragraph similarity by whether they reference either the same papers as the selected paragraph (primary sort-order), or are semantically similar papers (secondary sort-order, using a threshold on the Euclidean distances between their SPECTER paper embeddings [13])." (p. 7)

mechanisms.value: history-sensitive paragraph reranking for novel subtopic coverage
mechanisms.what_makes_it_separate: it changes the global order of paragraph cards from relevance alone toward diverse unread coverage; the badges and highlights below expose local reasons without performing that ordering.

quotes: "The goal is to re-rank the paragraphs such that the top paragraphs jointly contain the most number of unique and unexplored references and present a wide range of diverse subtopics, while accounting for their relevance to the query term and number of references." (p. 6)

mechanisms.value: dynamically updated unread-reference count per paragraph
mechanisms.value_canonical: VA059 Progress, coverage or completion tracking
mechanisms.what_makes_it_separate: the badge exposes a local numeric estimate of unread material for one paragraph; it does not reorder cards or identify which individual reference is dissimilar.

quotes: "Unexplored references count badge: Both our formative interviews and prior work pointed to wanting to prioritize paragraphs that had the highest unread information first." (p. 7)

VA059 Progress, coverage or completion tracking

quotes: "This number dynamically updates as the user interacts with more references across the paragraphs." (p. 7)

mechanisms.value: yellow-gradient highlighting of semantically dissimilar unread references
mechanisms.value_canonical: VA032 Attention directed to the spot that matters now
mechanisms.facet_canonical: FC043 attention direction and salience cueing
mechanisms.what_makes_it_separate: this marks individual citations by semantic difference from prior reading; the unread-count badge only quantifies novelty and the reranker changes global order.

quotes: "As the user clicks and reads references and paragraphs, some references get highlighted yellow indicating that these papers are semantically different to other papers interacted with so far (calculated using a threshold on the Euclidean distances between their SPECTER paper embeddings [13])." (p. 7)

VA032 Attention directed to the spot that matters now
FC043 attention direction and salience cueing
this marks individual citations by semantic difference from prior reading; the unread-count badge only quantifies novelty and the reranker changes global order.

quotes: "These references are highlighted on a yellow gradient, where the brighter the yellow, the highlighted paper is more different than the most similar papers interacted with so far." (p. 7)

mechanisms.value_canonical: VA096 Disclosure of origin, authorship or data handling
mechanisms.what_makes_it_separate: this represents temporal coverage and supports a recency-versus-foundational judgment, unlike novelty, similarity, or citation-frequency cues.

quotes: "Reference timeline visualization: Another heuristic that users wanted to use was to prioritize paragraphs that covered both recent and fundamental prior research on the topic." (p. 7)

entries.value: VA096 Disclosure of origin, authorship or data handling
this represents temporal coverage and supports a recency-versus-foundational judgment, unlike novelty, similarity, or citation-frequency cues.

quotes: "As the min and max of the timeline signify the earliest and latest papers referenced across all paragraphs, users can use this to prioritize reading paragraphs that reference recent papers or more fundamental older papers." (p. 7)

mechanisms.value_canonical: VA021 Aggregate statistic or distribution readout
mechanisms.what_makes_it_separate: this estimates a paper’s topical centrality from repeated citation across returned paragraphs; it does not encode publication time, semantic difference, or reading state.

quotes: "Citation frequency badges: Participants in the formative interviews mentioned wanting to prioritize parts of a paragraph, particularly wanting to know which paper to prioritize when there are multiple papers cited for a claim or in a paragraph." (p. 7)

entries.value: VA021 Aggregate statistic or distribution readout
this estimates a paper’s topical centrality from repeated citation across returned paragraphs; it does not encode publication time, semantic difference, or reading state.

quotes: "Relatedly offers Citation frequency badges that aim to indicate how central or important a referenced paper is to a topic." (p. 7)

mechanisms.value_canonical: VA096 Disclosure of origin, authorship or data handling
mechanisms.what_makes_it_separate: this identifies whose work or idea a passage and copied reference belongs to; the other reference cues encode novelty, age, or centrality instead.

quotes: "Self-reference icons: Participants in the formative interviews mentioned wanting to de-prioritize parts of a paragraph where the authors were situating their own work in the background." (p. 7)

entries.value: VA096 Disclosure of origin, authorship or data handling

quotes: "To avoid potential unintended consequences such as plagiarism, Relatedly’s design aims to highlight the provenance of ideas and encourage correct referencing practice by prioritizing author information at the top of paragraphs and attaching author information when users copy over references." (p. 16)

mechanisms.value_canonical: VA059 Progress, coverage or completion tracking
mechanisms.facet_canonical: FC079 external memory and recall cue
mechanisms.what_makes_it_separate: this automatically de-emphasizes redundant sentence-level material based on prior clicks; explicit paragraph marking and aggregate progress remain separate user actions and summaries.

quotes: "Relatedly also low-lights sentences that refer to papers that have been cited in already-seen paragraphs (e)." (p. 3)

entries.value: exploration in the baseline centered on individual papers rather than paragraph-level topics — (PDF p. 13)
quotes: "Participants described their exploration strategies were centered around individual papers instead of paragraphs when using the Baseline." (p. 13)

entries.value: users alternated between a broad paragraph overview and focused subtopic drill-downs — (PDF p. 12)
quotes: "All participants switched between the Overview View and Similar Paragraph View for broad overview and drill-down into different subtopics." (p. 12)

entries.value: scholars lacked clear cues for reading order, paragraph differences, and central papers — (PDF p. 5)
quotes: "Some participants desired prioritization and navigation support to know what to read next: “hard to prioritize which order to read these in” (5/10), “it is unclear what the similarities and differences between paragraphs are” (7/10), “want to know which are the most important or central papers summarized in this paragraph” (3/10)." (p. 5)

entries.value: users employed multiple paragraph and reference cues to prioritize novel or important material and de-prioritize redundancy — (PDF p. 13)
quotes: "Based on qualitative data, participants utilized the reading support cues to both prioritize and de-prioritize their reading activities." (p. 13)

entries.value: scholars could not reliably remember what they had read or assess remaining coverage — (PDF p. 5)
quotes: "Participants also wanted support for tracking their exploration: “want to keep track of what [paper and paragraph] has been read vs not” (2/10), “hard to assess how much more there is to read on this topic” (2/10)." (p. 5)

entries.value: users externalized encounter state, marked completed paragraphs, and monitored aggregate coverage; they rated tracking support higher than baseline — (PDF p. 15)
quotes: "Participants in the evaluation study agreed significantly more to the statements: the system helped me “find relevant research on the topic”, “understand relationships between terms/concepts”, “bring together information from multiple sources and points of view”, “prioritize what to read” and “keep track of information gained or read during the literature review process” compared to the Baseline system." (p. 15)

rq3_entries.value: organizing many related-work paragraphs into subtopic exploration, exposing reading-support cues, and tracking information gain — (PDF p. 17)
quotes: "Relatedly also provides reading support cues and information gain tracking features to facilitate users in reading many related work paragraphs to cover a broad overview of different topics more efficiently." (p. 17)

rq3_entries.value: querying, choosing what to inspect, judging relevance and context, and synthesizing an outline and notes — (PDF p. 10)
quotes: "During the study, participants used the assigned system to explore the literature with the goal of creating an outline and notes for writing a survey paper on assigned topics." (p. 10)

rq3_entries.value: author_raised — the authors warn that attention-management algorithms can mislead users and reinforce bias or echo chambers — (PDF p. 15)
quotes: "We believe that any system that uses algorithmic approaches to help user manage their attentions (recommendations, search, summarization), should be aware of and account for potential model errors misleading users, implicit biases, and echo chamber effects in their designs." (p. 15)

rq3_entries.value: no — exploration-state support persists across queries rather than decreasing with competence — (PDF p. 8)
quotes: "This remains persistent across queries, so as a user issues new queries and if they have read any of the papers or paragraphs before, these would would be tracked in the progress bar too." (p. 8)

rq3_entries.value: users must continue exploring sources and constructing the survey outline; the paper reports no reduction of these responsibilities as expertise grows — (PDF p. 10)
quotes: "During the task, write an outline in the notes document provided to you such that it would help you resume work on this task in the future." (p. 10)

"Therefore, we continued to allowed them access to Relatedly from their computers to conduct their own tasks, and scheduled interviews with them after two weeks to learn about their user experience." (p. 13)

claim_entries.value: Relatedly helped scholars synthesize a topic more broadly, coherently, and insightfully — (PDF p. 17)
quotes: "A comparative user study demonstrated that Relatedly’s approach to literature review helped scholars synthesize information on the topic in broader, more coherent and insightful manner." (p. 17)
"We compared Relatedly to a Baseline system simulating standard scholarly search engines as an within-subject condition." (p. 10)
"15 participants were recruited from research labs across three universities (8 identified as female and the rest as male; age: 19-32. M=25.88, SD=3.72)." (p. 11)
"The participants were mostly research scientists, post-docs, and graduate students engaging in research activities." (p. 11)
"The baseline condition was a standard BM25 search engine that returned a list of papers from our dataset that mentioned the query term in their titles or abstracts (Fig. 4)." (p. 10)

claim_entries.value: test_only — inferential tests and descriptive statistics were reported without an effect-size statistic — (PDF p. 14)
quotes: "For each statement, we report the percentage of likert responses and results from paired wilcoxon signed rank tests, with z and p values." (p. 14)
"Compensation was $45 USD for the 90 minute study." (p. 11)

claim_entries.value: perceived workload did not differ significantly between systems — (PDF p. 13)
quotes: "Lastly, to measure the perceived workload of using the two systems, we used the NASA TLX questionnaire, and found no significant differences (Appendix Table 5)." (p. 13)

claim_entries.value: blinded expert ratings in the within-subject comparison support the claimed improvement in synthesized-outline quality within the tested tasks — (PDF p. 3)
quotes: "We find that participants produced better quality outlines when using Relatedly versus in the baseline condition, as rated by topic experts who were blind to the conditions." (p. 3)

paper_code_entries.value: scientific literature review and survey-outline construction — (PDF p. 10)
quotes: "During the study, participants used the assigned system to explore the literature with the goal of creating an outline and notes for writing a survey paper on assigned topics." (p. 10)

paper_code_entries.value: immediate_performance_or_sensemaking — support targets an immediate overview and literature-review task rather than durable skill development — (PDF p. 5)
quotes: "Guided by the insights from our formative study, we developed Relatedly, a novel approach to literature review that helps users achieve a broader and more insightful overview of a research topic." (p. 5)

paper_code_entries.value: novice_or_learner — the design centers junior researchers entering an unfamiliar topic — (PDF p. 16)
quotes: "Since Relatedly aims to help people jump-start their lit review process by broadly overviewing and finding relevant papers in an unknown topic, we focused on understanding the needs of junior researchers." (p. 16)

paper_code_entries.value: coordination_or_memory_gap — users struggled to prioritize and retain exploration state across papers — (PDF p. 3)
quotes: "For example, when exploring papers from a search results list, it can be hard for users to prioritize their readings, keep track of information scattered across multiple papers, or have a sense of their overall progress within the unfamiliar information space." (p. 3)

paper_code_entries.value: process — interaction logs measured paragraph-level and paper-level exploration — (PDF p. 11)
quotes: "Using the behavior logs from both conditions, we measured how frequently each participant interacted with both the systems at both the paragraphs and papers level." (p. 11)

paper_code_entries.value: artifact — experts assessed the outlines participants produced — (PDF p. 11)
quotes: "The experts counted the number of research themes participants added to their outlines (a proxy for comprehensiveness), and rated the outlines for the following aspects on a five-point scale (higher is better):" (p. 11)

paper_code_entries.value: structuring — paragraph titles expose gist and subtopic organization — (PDF p. 7)
quotes: "Each paragraph in the Overview View comes with a descriptive title to describe the gist of the paragraph’s focus and serve as a subtopic for the user." (p. 7)

paper_code_entries.value: problematizing — the interface deliberately surfaces dissimilar information instead of only reinforcing similarity — (PDF p. 15)
quotes: "Further, while most prior recommender systems help users in finding documents similar to what they have already explored, Relatedly, in contrast, actively re-ranks documents and highlight sentences to encourage users to prioritize exploring information most dissimilar to what they have already explored." (p. 15)

paper_code_entries.value: contingency — unread-information cues respond to ongoing interaction — (PDF p. 7)
quotes: "This number dynamically updates as the user interacts with more references across the paragraphs." (p. 7)

paper_code_entries.value: adaptation — paragraph presentation changes from the user’s accumulated exploration history — (PDF p. 5)
quotes: "She notices that the paragraphs she is shown have changed as a result of her exploration thus far." (p. 5)
"Paragraphs have been dynamically re-ranked to prioritize ones with more unexplored and dissimilar references." (p. 5)

paper_code_entries.value: distributed_support — the scaffold repurposes organizational work contributed by many prior authors — (PDF p. 17)
quotes: "The idea here is that by leveraging prior scientific efforts of authors conducting literature reviews to write their related work sections, we can improve other researchers’ literature review process." (p. 17)

paper_code_entries.value: hybrid_or_multi_model — semantic organization combines SPECTER similarity with BART-generated headings — (PDF pp. 7–8)
quotes: "We determine paragraph similarity by whether they reference either the same papers as the selected paragraph (primary sort-order), or are semantically similar papers (secondary sort-order, using a threshold on the Euclidean distances between their SPECTER paper embeddings [13])." (p. 7)

"To address this, we developed an automated heading generation model, trained on heuristically identified descriptive section headings, and applied it to paragraphs that did not have descriptive headings written by the authors of the source paper." (p. 8)

paper_code_entries.value: pre_llm_ai — the generative path uses pre-LLM sequence-to-sequence models — (PDF p. 8)
quotes: "We experimented with two popular transformer-based sequence-to-sequence models for heading generation: (i) BART [42], and (ii) T5 [59]." (p. 8)

limitations: "One assumption we made was that scientists write high quality related work sections in their paper that can provide more benefits to users than looking at individual papers and synthesizing them." (p. 16)
"Future work can build on our study by including prior visualization systems as a baseline to compare Relatedly against to help us further understand the costs and benefits of Relatedly." (p. 16)
"In the formative interviews, we mostly interviewed PhD students who are junior scholars." (p. 16)
"One potential obstacle to broader adoption of this approach is licensing and access to scientific documents." (p. 16)

"While our user evaluation lab study observed how Relatedly helped participants explore information on a single topic and query, an exciting avenue for future work is investigating how users shift their exploration over multiple topics and queries." (p. 16)
boundary_conditions: "For this, we selected papers from leading venues in HCI and NLP to construct our dataset." (p. 16)
"Currently, Relatedly is designed for scholarly users." (p. 16)
